title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel language model architecture that scales test-time computation by implicitly reasoning in latent space. The model works by iterating a recurrent block, allowing it to unroll to arbitrary depth at test-time.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You don't just write down the answer, you think about it, using mental models and abstractions. Our model works in a similar way, using latent reasoning to solve problems. This approach allows the model to scale up test-time computation without requiring specialized training data or large context windows.

By using a recurrent block, the model can iterate to arbitrary depth, enabling it to capture types of reasoning that are not easily represented in words.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The model consists of three main components: the prelude, the recurrent block, and the coda. The prelude embeds the input into a latent space, the recurrent block iterates to refine the representation, and the coda produces the output.

The recurrent block is the core of the model, allowing it to scale up test-time computation. By using a log-normal Poisson distribution to sample the number of recurrent iterations, the model can adapt to different problem sizes and complexities.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated our model on several benchmark datasets, including ARC challenge, GSM8K, and OpenBookQA. The results show that our model can improve its performance on reasoning benchmarks, sometimes dramatically, up to a computation load equivalent to 50 billion parameters.

The model achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of latent reasoning for scaling up test-time computation.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Our approach has several advantages over traditional methods. It does not require specialized training data or large context windows, and it can capture types of reasoning that are not easily represented in words.

Additionally, the model can be trained with a variable compute budget, using standard training data with no specialized demonstrations, and enhance its abilities at test-time if given additional compute.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our approach introduces several key innovations, including the use of a recurrent block to scale up test-time computation, and the use of a log-normal Poisson distribution to sample the number of recurrent iterations.

These innovations enable the model to capture types of reasoning that are not easily represented in words, and to improve its performance on reasoning benchmarks.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
We provide a publicly available implementation of our model, along with pretraining code and intermediate model checkpoints.

You can try out our model on your own dataset, and explore the capabilities of latent reasoning for scaling up test-time computation.
